advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the _shadow() call in bridge_projects_set/remove to before `with lock.write_lock(tracker):` so shadow composition does not extend lock-hold time.
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:163-164: same pattern for bridge_projects_remove inside `with lock.write_lock(tracker):`
Contrast: in bridge_fsck/bridge_projects_list/etc. _shadow is called before any lock is acquired.
advisory.finding: In _lib_ops.bridge_projects_set/bridge_projects_remove the shadow-snapshot call is placed INSIDE the write_lock context manager, so the snapshot composition (TOML parse + potential git subprocess via resolve_with_sources/repo_root) runs while the store write lock is held, needlessly extending lock-hold duration. Every other library operation calls _shadow OUTSIDE any lock.
advisory.suggested_fix: Emit the shadow snapshot before acquiring the write lock, e.g. call `_shadow(repo_root, ...)` right after computing `root`/`tracker` and before the `with lock.write_lock(tracker):` block, matching the other library ops.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the _shadow() call out of the ValueError/KeyError-guarded try block in bridge_projects_set/remove so a diagnostic fault can never be mistaken for a bridge error.
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:141-146: `try:` / `with lock.write_lock(tracker): _shadow(...)` / `except ValueError as exc: raise _invalid_bridge(str(exc))`
emit_shadow_snapshot swallows Exception (src/rebar/_operation_config.py:252) so no leak today — this is a latent fragility, not an active bug.
advisory.finding: The shadow call in _lib_ops.bridge_projects_set/remove sits inside the try block guarded by `except ValueError`/`except KeyError`; because ConfigError subclasses ValueError, any leaked exception from the shadow path would be misclassified as a bridge error. emit_shadow_snapshot currently catches all exceptions internally so nothing leaks today, but placing a diagnostic inside a semantically-meaningful except is fragile against future edits.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drive the MCP tool layer and the reconciler entry point through their real seams (e.g. register the MCP tools / call rebar_reconciler.main) so the AC1 equivalence assertion exercises actual per-surface wiring rather than three identical compose_operation_snapshot calls.
evidence: Comment '# MCP surface: composes once per operation from the same neutral contract.' but no MCP tool is registered/invoked; docstring AC1 claims equivalence 'through CLI, public Python, MCP, and the direct reconciler entry point'
advisory.finding: The AC1 cross-surface equivalence test does not drive the MCP or reconciler entry points; it calls compose_operation_snapshot(repo_root=str(p), cli_overrides=overrides) three times with identical arguments and labels them 'Python', 'MCP', and 'reconciler' surfaces, then asserts they are equal. This is asserting f(x) == f(x) for the MCP and reconciler legs — a tautology that exercises none of the actual MCP tool wiring (_shadow in _mcp_reads/_mcp_writes/_mcp_llm) or the reconciler _emit_operation_shadow/main wiring. It cannot detect a regression that miswires those surfaces (wrong repo_root, wrong/missing surface, dropped call).
scenarios: A refactor drops or misconfigures the emit_shadow_snapshot/_shadow call in an MCP tool or the reconciler entry point
The reconciler passes the wrong repo_root or surface to emit_shadow_snapshot

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider gating the CLI shadow emit behind the effective log level / a cheaper root, or accept the per-invocation git subprocess cost explicitly (temporary S1 wiring).
evidence: src/rebar/_config_sources.py:40-46: repo_root falls through to `subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], ...)` when explicit and REBAR_ROOT are absent
emit_shadow_snapshot also calls resolve_with_sources which parses project/user TOML each invocation
dropped.finding: The CLI shadow emit is invoked with no repo_root on every invocation; when REBAR_ROOT is unset, _config_sources.repo_root spawns a `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` subprocess for the shadow diagnostic on EVERY CLI call — including help/version and non-store commands that otherwise do no git work — adding a new per-invocation startup cost.

evidence: search for emit_shadow_snapshot / _emit_operation_shadow shows call sites only in src/ and no test invoking them except the CLI main() in the interface test
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:625 'from rebar._operation_config import emit_shadow_snapshot' inside try/except Exception: pass at line ~628
_lib_ops.py, _mcp_reads.py, _mcp_writes.py, _mcp_llm.py each define a local _shadow(...) helper called at every tool/op, none referenced from tests
dropped.finding: The shadow-mode wiring inserted at every surface — the ~50 _shadow(...) call sites across _mcp_reads.py/_mcp_writes.py/_mcp_llm.py, the _shadow helper in _lib_ops.py, the CLI emit_shadow_snapshot(surface="cli"), the command-seam emit_shadow_snapshot(surface="command-write"), and the reconciler _emit_operation_shadow wrapper — has no test that invokes those paths and asserts the shadow fires. Only emit_shadow_snapshot itself and the CLI path are exercised. The reconciler wrapper's swallow-all-exceptions boundary (bare except Exception: pass around the import+call) is entirely untested, so a broken import or a wiring error there would be silent.
